critical_code_review_comments: Referral code generator uses secrets.token_urlsafe(4) then strips '_'/'-' and slices to 6 chars — under unlucky entropy this could produce a string slightly shorter than 6 chars in edge cases (token_urlsafe(4) returns 6-7 chars; after replaces it's always >=6). Acceptable but a fixed alphabet random_choice(6) would be more deterministic.

Rate-limit bucket is in-memory and global (module-level dict). Won't survive process restarts and is shared across all workers in a single process; under multi-worker uvicorn each worker has its own bucket which effectively multiplies the limit by worker count. For production deploy behind multiple workers, move to Redis or DB-backed limiter.

Referral self-referral guard compares the entered code with the NEW customer's own auto-generated code — but the new customer's code was just generated in this request, so the user can't possibly know it. The guard is harmless but doesn't actually prevent the realistic abuse case (a returning customer using their own code on a second phone) since the function only credits brand-new customers anyway.

Invoice referral_credit consumption is computed BEFORE tax (correct), but the credit decrement uses $inc with a negative value — if the customer document later goes below 0 due to a race condition (two simultaneous invoice POSTs), referral_credit could go negative. Acceptable for a salon-scale app, flag for future.
Stock-check loop in /api/invoices does an await per product (N+1 queries). For larger carts, a single $in find would be more efficient.

Backend business-hours validator uses ist.hour < 10 or ist.hour >= 21, which rejects 21:00 exactly. The spec says 'between 10:00 AM and 9:00 PM' which is ambiguous about inclusivity — current behavior allows 20:30 but blocks 21:00. Acceptable.
